agent.result_text:
All tests pass — BUILD SUCCESS.

## Summary

I changed the `customerCode` format from `'<LAST3>-<NNNN>'` to `'<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>'` in `OwnerRestControllerV1.java`:

- **`generateCustomerCode`** now takes both `city` and `lastName`. It builds `CITY3` (upper-cased first three letters of the city), `LAST3` (upper-cased first three of the last name), and `NNNN`, a **per-city** 4-digit sequence equal to one more than the owners already in that city (previously a global count).
- Added two helpers: `first3Letters` (shared by the city and last-name segments, mirroring the original letter-stripping logic) and `countOwnersInCity` (counts existing owners by city, comparing case- and whitespace-insensitively, consistent with the existing namesake/household comparisons).
- Updated the call site in `addOwner` to pass `owner.getCity()`.

Everything derived from `customerCode` rebuilds automatically: `Owner.getMembershipNumber()` formats `'<customerCode>-M<YY>'` directly from the stored code, so it now carries the new format (e.g. `SYD-SMI-0007-M26`) with no change needed there. No other code hardcodes the old format.

The acceptance test `coreCustomerCodeHasCityPrefix` (asserting the `[A-Z]{3}-[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}` pattern) and the full suite pass.

code_review.final_verdict:
VERDICT: LGTM

The change is clean, additive, and idiomatic for this codebase:

- **Shared logic extracted correctly.** The previously inlined "strip non-letters, take first three, upper-case" logic is pulled into `first3Letters` and reused for both the city and last-name segments, removing what would otherwise have been a copy-paste duplication.
- **New helper mirrors the established pattern.** `countOwnersInCity` is structured exactly like the existing `countNamesakes` (stream over `findAllOwners()`, compare via `normalizeForComparison`, `count()`), so a maintainer will find it immediately familiar. Using `normalizeForComparison` for the city keeps it consistent with every other owner-field comparison in the class.
- **Logic is in the right unit.** Code-generation stays in the controller's private helpers alongside `generateCustomerCode`, `countNamesakes`, and the household helpers — the same altitude as the surrounding code.
- **Derived values are handled without needing a change here.** The membership number is computed on the fly in `Owner.getMembershipNumber()` from `customerCode`, so it is automatically rebuilt on the new format; nothing structural was missed.
- **Documentation matches the file's conventions.** The Javadoc on the new/changed methods is as thorough and consistently styled as the rest of the class.

No duplication, no catch-all growth, no misplaced logic.
